s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with rash and hypotension in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: erythematous patches and thin plaques with telangiectases and hyperpigmentation
intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy
key_facts: patient has a history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis
patient was being treated with fluconazole
pembrolizumab treatment was stopped 3 months prior due to a morbilliform reaction
new skin eruption appeared different from previous reaction
patient has fever and hypotension
white blood cell count is 4100/μL
absolute neutrophil count is 2940/μL
hemoglobin level is 8.2 g/dL
platelet count is 62 ×10^3/μL
blood culture results showed no growth at 1 week
serum β-D-glucan, galactomannan, Coccidioides antibody, and immunodiffusion results were negative

shortlist.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Skin biopsy findings showing intravascular atypical cells

shortlist.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Fever, hypotension, and cytopenias in an immunocompromised patient

shortlist.label: Cytokine release syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of pembrolizumab treatment and new skin eruption

shortlist.label: Natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised state and skin eruption with atypical cells

raw.rationale: The presence of intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy, as shown by hematoxylin-eosin stained sections and CD56 immunostaining, is a key diagnostic feature of intravascular large B-cell lymphoma. The patient's symptoms, including fever, hypotension, and a new skin eruption, along with laboratory findings such as anemia (low hemoglobin level) and thrombocytopenia (low platelet count), also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
rejected.why: While this condition can present with similar systemic symptoms, the specific finding of intravascular atypical cells on biopsy is more indicative of intravascular large B-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Cytokine release syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is typically associated with a recent history of immunotherapy or a significant immune response, but the patient's pembrolizumab treatment was stopped 3 months prior, making this less likely.

rejected.label: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
rejected.why: Although the patient has thrombocytopenia, the presence of intravascular atypical cells and the specific skin biopsy findings point more towards a lymphoma diagnosis rather than a primary coagulopathy.

rejected.label: Natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While this is a type of lymphoma, the specific biopsy findings and the clinical presentation are more consistent with intravascular large B-cell lymphoma, which is characterized by the presence of large B-cells within the blood vessels.
